newsitem.title: USA: Possible remains in Calif. cremation case found.
newsitem.headline: Possible remains in Calif. cremation case found.

text.p: Authorities said on Wednesday they had found a decomposed body believed to be that of pilot Allan Vieira, who allegedly put thousands of boxes of cremated human remains in storage after he was hired to spread them over mountains and at sea.
Investigators have been searching for weeks for the pilot, who operates the Vieira Flying Service. Authorities believe he was hired by funeral homes in California to spread the ashes.

Instead, sheriff's deputies said he placed more than 5,000 boxes of the cremated remains in public storage lockers in Discovery Bay, about 45 miles (72 km) east of San Francisco, and at a nearby hangar where he kept a plane. The macabre discovery of the remains traumatized families of the deceased, shocked California residents and baffled investigators.

The badly decomposed body and a handgun were found just south of San Andreas, about 100 miles (160 km) east of San Francisco, near an abandoned car believed to have been driven by Vieira. Boxes of cremated remains were found in the car along with a note saying "Sorry for the pain I've caused!"
Investigators have not ruled the death a suicide. "We're not going to assume it was a suicide until we can have an autopsy and rule out other things," Detective Ethel Mitchell said.
The body has yet to be positively identified. Coroners will use Vieira's dental records to try to make the match.
Many of the boxes of ashes had name tags and dates, identifying the deceased and when they were cremated. Investigators have been able to return some of the ashes to their families.
